text:
anya: Heads up — bringing up an HF SentencePiece model through our HF->Redwood conversion. Seeing token-id drift after conversion and a measurable quality drop once we run int8. TL;DR: tokens shifted, special tokens duplicated, ppl +7% after quant.
sam: can you paste the tokenizer/config.json and the conversion command you used?
anya: sure — conversion was basically the quick script: `python tools/hf_to_redwood.py --src hf-spm-model --out /tmp/redwood` then `redwood-deploy convert-tokenizer /tmp/redwood` but the tokenizer config looked like this:

```json
{
  "tokenizer_class": "SentencePieceTokenizer",
  "model_max_length": 2048,
  "bos_token": "<s>",
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "unk_token": "<unk>",
  "pad_token": "<pad>",
  "special_tokens": ["<s>","</s>","<pad>","<unk>"]
}
```

sam: hmm. SP models don't have merges; when you "convert" to a BPE/merges-based format we either create synthetic merges or use a fallback tokenizer. That can change tokenization boundaries and token ids. Did the conversion script remap special token IDs or just append new ones?
anya: it appended. I see the original HF vocab size 50280, our converted BPE vocab 50286. Special tokens got new high-ids instead of preserving originals. Example: originally `<pad>` id=1, after convert `<pad>` id=50285 and old id=1 is now a generic token. Lots of examples where `tokenizer.decode([orig_id])` != original string.
ben: that's the root cause. Model weights expect the original token id layout in the embedding matrix. If conversion only changes tokenizer->new ids without remapping embeddings, embedding lookup becomes inconsistent.
ben: quick checks:
- run `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf-spm-model')` and inspect `tokenizer.get_vocab()`
- compare to `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(tokenizer.all_special_tokens)`
- ensure we call `model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))` with proper mapping or remap embeddings to new ids.

mira: for quantization: we ran two experiments:
- naive int8 (global symmetric): latency +12% but ppl +7% (bad)
- int8 with Embedding/LayerNorm excluded: latency +8% and ppl +1% (acceptable)

mira: command we used:
```
python tools/quantize.py --model /tmp/redwood --dtype int8 --calib_samples 2048 --out /tmp/redwood-int8
```
with `--skip-embeddings` toggled for the second run.

anya: also saw chat-template mismatch. HF chat template used role tokens like `<|system|>`, `<|user|>`. Our Redwood chat preset expects serialized JSON messages or the classic `<s> role` pair. So converted prompt strings had extra tokens inserted and token offsets changed.
sam: two follow-ups:
1) For tokenizer conversion, change script to preserve special token ids by mapping: create a new tokenizer that uses HF tokenization outputs (fast tokenizers) but write a `vocab.json` where special_token->original_id preserved. That way embeddings align.
2) For spm->bpe, instead of creating merges, prefer saving the HF SentencePiece model (.model) and use a SentencePieceTokenizer in Redwood runtime; only fallback to BPE if there is a strict requirement.

ben: other edge-case: Unknown token normalization. Some SP vocab uses byte-fallbacks and normalization pre-tokenization (NFKC) that BPE fast tokenizers may skip. That causes differences in token counts for punctuation-heavy prompts used in our NLU evals.

anya: results from eval-bot run (small summary):
- eval suite: lm-perplexity on 5 heldout datasets; ddp=deterministic seed
- HF original float32: avg ppl 12.3
- converted + float32 (no remap): avg ppl 13.1
- converted + remapped embeddings: avg ppl 12.4
- converted + quant int8 (naive): avg ppl 13.5
- converted + quant int8 (skip-embeddings): avg ppl 12.5

eval-bot: posted detailed logs to the run: https://internal/runs/2026/conv-spm-171068

mira: action items I propose:
- sam to update conversion script to preserve special token ids OR output a mapping file so we can remap embedding rows (owner: sam, ETA 2d)
- ben to add optional path in quantize that excludes Emb/LayerNorm or does per-channel quant for MatMul weights (owner: ben, ETA 3d)
- anya to add a test in the HF->Redwood onboarding CI that loads 1 sample prompt and compares tokenization to HF reference (owner: anya, ETA 1d)

sam: noted. I'll also add a quick diff utility: `python tools/tokenizer_diff.py hf-spm-model /tmp/redwood` that prints first 5k token id->string comparisons and highlights mismatches.
anya: thanks. One small note — we should also check chat templates mapping for function-calling and tool-spec prompts; those rely on exact token offsets in a few downstream evals.
ben: :thumbsup: good plan.

mira: filing a short postmortem in the onboarding board with links to the conversion script, quant logs, and the eval runs.
anya: thanks everyone — will block time to review sam's patch once ready.

eval-bot: automated note: run `conv-spm-171068` completed. artifacts: tokenizer_diff.txt, ppl_breakdown.csv, quant_stats.json
